principle: IMA learns from both similar and fundamentally different systems; lessons are adapted, never blindly copied.

similar_systems.lesson: agentic browser research and multi-tab task execution
similar_systems.adaptation: strengthen LIVE-001 browser grounding while preserving explicit approval

similar_systems.lesson: persistent agents with memory and skills
similar_systems.adaptation: strengthen IMA memory provenance and user-controlled lifecycle without creating a second memory authority

similar_systems.lesson: triggered work across email/calendar/meetings with approvals
similar_systems.adaptation: connect future IMA action contracts to user-approved workflows
apply governance and observability before expanding IMA automation

similar_systems.lesson: deep integration with existing work context and permissions
similar_systems.adaptation: design permission-scoped connectors rather than broad account access

fundamentally_different_systems.lesson: device-level continuity, accessibility and privacy architecture
fundamentally_different_systems.adaptation: treat device continuity and accessibility as first-class IMA layers
reuse composability concept under IMA's single canonical runtime

fundamentally_different_systems.lesson: enterprise automation, observability and process governance
fundamentally_different_systems.adaptation: extend IMA auditability without adopting enterprise-style autonomous execution
keep future device/robot/space interfaces behind the same permission and safety contracts

fundamentally_different_systems.lesson: interaction should remain usable when conventional UI fails
fundamentally_different_systems.adaptation: make accessibility-tree and multimodal fallback a core IMA capability

not_promoted.reason: Product-specific features, pricing, branding, proprietary implementations and claims without reproducible evidence are not imported as capabilities.
